actions.justification: Mandatory first step to establish chief complaint, symptom duration, functional class, medication history, and baseline for HFrEF management.
Mandatory physical exam to assess for signs of congestion (JVD, rales, edema), hemodynamic status, and volume overload in this HFrEF patient.
Mandatory ECG to evaluate for arrhythmias, conduction abnormalities, ischemia, or QRS duration relevant to CRT candidacy in HFrEF.
Mandatory lab to assess renal function, electrolytes, and glucose in HFrEF patient, within 60-minute deadline.
Mandatory biomarker to quantify severity of heart failure and guide management decisions.
Mandatory lab to evaluate for anemia or infection contributing to heart failure decompensation.
Mandatory action - chest X-ray is essential in HFrEF to assess for pulmonary congestion, cardiomegaly, and pleural effusions. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.
Mandatory action - TSH is indicated in HFrEF workup to identify thyroid dysfunction as a reversible cause or contributor to heart failure. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.

Assessing the hemodynamic profile (wet/dry, warm/cold) in this HFrEF patient will guide treatment decisions regarding diuretics, vasodilators, and other therapies. Patient appears stable but full hemodynamic profiling is standard of care.
Patient has HFrEF with EF below 40% - formal LVEF assessment is essential to guide guideline-directed medical therapy and device therapy decisions.
Patient with HFrEF (EF <40%) should be evaluated for ICD implantation per heart failure guidelines for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death.
Patient with HFrEF should be assessed for CRT candidacy based on QRS duration/morphology and LVEF to potentially improve cardiac function and outcomes.

Patient has HFrEF with EF below 40%. NYHA functional class assessment is essential to guide therapy decisions including ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA dosing, and candidacy for advanced therapies like CRT or ICD. This has not yet been completed.

Assessing for structural abnormalities (e.g., valvular disease, wall motion abnormalities) is important in HFrEF management to identify potentially reversible or treatable etiologies and guide further management.
Given HFrEF with EF <40%, patient should be evaluated for advanced therapies such as cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), LVAD, or transplant based on clinical trajectory and NYHA class.

Patient has HFrEF with EF below 40% and hypertension. With stable vitals, it is important to assess whether the patient is on optimal guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) duration and dosing, including ACE inhibitor/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, and MRA, to guide next treatment steps.
HFrEF patient should be evaluated for congestion. If signs of fluid overload are present, diuretic therapy (e.g., furosemide) is a cornerstone of HF management per guidelines.
Cardiac rehabilitation is recommended for stable HFrEF patients (NYHA class II-III) to improve functional capacity, quality of life, and reduce hospitalizations per ACC/AHA HF guidelines.
Confirm whether patient is on optimal guideline-directed medical therapy for HFrEF with EF<40%. This is a key step before adding or adjusting medications.

ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI is a Class I recommendation for all patients with HFrEF (EF<40%) to reduce mortality and morbidity. Patient is hemodynamically stable with BP 120/80, making this appropriate.
Beta-blocker therapy (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, or bisoprolol) is a Class I recommendation for HFrEF with EF<40% to reduce mortality. HR is 80 and BP is stable, making initiation appropriate.
MRA (e.g., spironolactone/eplerenone) is recommended GDMT for HFrEF with EF <40% to reduce mortality and hospitalizations, and has not yet been addressed.
Ivabradine is indicated for HFrEF patients in sinus rhythm with HR ≥70 bpm on maximally tolerated beta-blocker; this patient's HR of 80 may qualify.
If congestion persists despite loop diuretic, adding a thiazide-type diuretic (combination/sequential nephron blockade) can enhance diuresis in resistant cases.
